evidence.finding: Billing queue skill mappings were updated at 09:15, exactly when the incident began.
At 09:15 Billing staffing dropped from 12 to 9 agents while General Service increased from 19 to 22; Billing remained at 9 through 11:45.
Scheduled and logged-in staffing remained constant at 49 agents throughout the window, showing redistribution rather than a center-wide staffing loss.
After the change, Billing service level fell to 14.8% at 09:15 and remained repeatedly far below target, while General Service stayed approximately 94.4%-97.1%.
Billing repeatedly received more calls than it answered, including 29 offered versus 15 answered at 09:15, 31 versus 18 at 09:30, and 30 versus 17 at 10:45.
Billing ASA rose from 32.1 seconds at 09:00 to 131.2 seconds at 09:15 and remained elevated for much of the incident.
Overall service level dropped from 93.0% at 09:00 to 67.1% at 09:15 and 59.1% at 09:30, with repeated later intervals below the 80% target.
Demand exceeded forecast at incident onset—87 versus 79 calls at 09:15 and 96 versus 79 at 09:30—but total post-incident demand was only modestly above forecast overall.

primary_root_cause_detail: The 09:15 Billing skill-mapping update immediately redistributed queue capacity: Billing staffing fell from 12 to 9 agents while General Service rose from 19 to 22, with total staffing unchanged. Billing then developed sustained excess demand relative to throughput, sharply elevated ASA, and severe service-level degradation.
recommended_actions: Rollback or correct the 09:15 Billing skill-mapping change and validate every affected skill-to-queue assignment.
Restore adequate Billing-skilled capacity and rebalance agents from General Service until the Billing backlog and ASA normalize.
Add pre-deployment validation and post-change alerts for abrupt queue staffing shifts, service-level divergence, and offered-versus-answered accumulation.
Review routing-change governance, including approval, testing, rollback criteria, and queue-level capacity impact checks.
Account for moderate interval-level volume variance in Billing staffing buffers without treating it as the primary cause.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Volume increases were moderate and intermittent, while the sustained failure was localized to Billing and began exactly with the routing change.
Center-wide staffing was stable at 49 scheduled and logged-in agents; the evidence shows queue-level redistribution rather than lost headcount.
Adherence remained within its existing 89.8%-93.9% range and did not show a sustained decline aligned with the incident.
Overall AHT was stable to lower than forecast during most affected intervals, and Billing AHT did not exhibit a sustained increase sufficient to explain the degradation.
No agents were in training during any interval.
No platform event was reported, and unaffected queues continued processing calls normally.
Forecast variance was not large or sustained enough to explain the severe, Billing-specific performance divergence.
The reported aggregate service-level values reconcile to the supplied formula, and the degradation is corroborated by ASA, abandonment, throughput, and queue-level results.

stakeholder_summary: CC-005 was caused by the 09:15 Billing routing configuration change, which shifted capacity away from Billing despite stable total staffing. Billing immediately accumulated calls and experienced sharply higher ASA and severe service-level degradation; moderate demand above forecast amplified the initial impact but was not the primary cause.
